info.name: Retail API (toys & flowers)
info.description:
Run with the Collection Runner (top to bottom). Prerequisites: Keycloak configured, ./retail-api/scripts/setup-keycloak-api-test.sh then ./retail-api/scripts/setup-keycloak-duns-clients.sh executed, retail-api running on http://localhost:8090.

Every token request names the DUNS (client_id = retail-duns-<DUNS> plus that client's own client_secret) and the resource (scope = "openid <DUNS>:<ROLE>", e.g. "openid 111111111:RETAILUI"). Keycloak then returns ONLY that role of that DUNS. Request names show the client and scope used; the console shows which roles each token carries.

| DUNS | Client id | Owns | Scope for RETAILUI |
|---|---|---|---|
| 111111111 | retail-duns-111111111 | toys | 111111111:RETAILUI |
| 222222222 | retail-duns-222222222 | flowers | 222222222:RETAILUI |

## Variant: one scope per DUNS, role chosen by `resource=` (folders 7-9)

The scope `duns-<DUNS>` contains ALL roles of that DUNS. The token request's `resource` parameter says which role(s) to issue, and a custom Keycloak mapper (keycloak-extensions/resource-role-mapper) removes every other role. Prerequisites: `keycloak-extensions/resource-role-mapper/deploy.sh`, then `retail-api/scripts/setup-keycloak-duns-resource-scopes.sh`.

| DUNS | Client id | Scope | Example request |
|---|---|---|---|
| 111111111 | retail-duns-111111111 | duns-111111111 | scope=`openid duns-111111111` resource=`RETAILUI` |
| 222222222 | retail-duns-222222222 | duns-222222222 | scope=`openid duns-222222222` resource=`RETAILUI CRR` |

No `resource` means no role. Several roles are space separated (Keycloak rejects a repeated `resource` parameter).
